findings.evidence: The sole proof occurrence is line 199, `have hNtriv := hN.nontrivial`; no indecomposability property of `N` is otherwise used.
findings.fix: Replace `hN` with `[Nontrivial N]` and remove that argument from callers.
findings.issue: `exists_linearEquiv_and_isCompl_biSup_ne` assumes `hN : IsIndecomposableModule A N`, but only uses `hN.nontrivial`; locality is already a separate hypothesis.

findings.evidence: Lines 116–119 are the only substantive use of the ambient chain conditions: they construct `IsLocalRing (Module.End A (P i₀))` via `isLocalRing_end_of_isIndecomposable`; the exchange lemma itself already accepts locality directly.
findings.fix: Prove the general theorem with `∀ i, IsLocalRing (Module.End A (P i))` (transporting locality across the linear equivalences in the induction), then derive the finite-length/Noetherian-Artinian theorem as a corollary.
findings.issue: The main uniqueness theorem assumes both `IsNoetherian` and `IsArtinian`, although the induction uses them only to establish that each selected `P i` has a local endomorphism ring; the natural Azumaya uniqueness theorem applies whenever those endomorphism rings are local.

summary: The exchange lemma has a visibly stronger hypothesis than its proof needs, and the uniqueness API unnecessarily hard-codes finite length instead of exposing the natural local-endomorphism-ring theorem.
